items.excerpt: Israeli attacks kill at least 10 Palestinians: At least 10 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza despite the ongoing ceasefire, according to health officials. Among the dead are senior Education Ministry official Khaled Abu Nada and his wife, killed in an air strike in Deir el-Balah. Six others were wounded, several critically. UK net migration drops: Net migration to the UK has fallen to 77,000, its lowest level since 1997 outside the pandemic, according to official figures released on Thursday (November 26). The figure dropped from 204,000 a year earlier and a record 906,000 in 2023. Indians remained the largest nationality group among long-term immigrants and emigrants. Bangkok refinery blast: An explosion at Bangchak Corporation's Phra Khanong oil refinery in Bangkok injured nine people, including three in critical condition. The blast triggered a fire at around 2.45 pm local time on Thursday. The company said the blaze was extinguished within 30 minutes, while authorities launched an investigation into the cause.

items.title: Cautious consumers gear up for Black Friday as inflation woes bite By Reuters
items.excerpt: NEW YORK/LOS ANGELES, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Neither high fuel prices nor stubborn inflation are expected to stop US shoppers from spending robustly as their turkey hangovers wear off on Black Friday. But below healthy top-line forecasts lie signs of stress. Holiday spending — which unofficially begins on Black Friday — is seen topping last year’s strong figures by 4%-6%, several economic forecasts show. But most of the gains will be attributable to inflation which, at 3.8%, is about a percentage point higher than in each of the last two years. The National Retail Federation sees November-December holiday retail sales rising 4.2% year-over-year, to just above $1 trillion. The Mastercard Economics Institute and EY Parthenon each forecast sales to rise more than 5%.

items.title: US economy roars ahead in third quarter, inflation remains high in October By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 25 (Reuters) - The US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, while inflation increased further in October, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027. The sharp upward revision to gross domestic product last quarter, reported by the Commerce Department on Wednesday, marked the quickest economic growth pace in three years. It reflected upgrades to consumer spending and business investment, mostly related to artificial intelligence. Robust domestic demand is fueling inflation, with a measure of underlying price pressures in October posting its biggest year-over-year increase since late 2023. The economy has powered ahead despite the ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran. ... Growth in consumer spending, which accounts for more than two-thirds of the economy, was revised up to a 4.2% rate. That was the strongest pace since the fourth quarter of 2024 and was an upgrade from the previously reported 3.8% pace. Spending is being driven mostly by higher-income households, whose wealth was boosted by the stock market before the ongoing AI-led selloff. ... PCE inflation was lifted by higher prices for goods, including food and household furnishings, as well as services such as recreation, dining out and hotel stays.

items.title: GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 | U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA)
items.excerpt: EST, Wednesday, November 25, 2026 # GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 4.3 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the second estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased. Real GDP was revised up 0.9 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting upward revisions to investment and consumer spending. For more information, refer to the " Technical Notes" below. Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in the third quarter primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports. Imports increased more in the third quarter than in the second quarter. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, the sum of consumer spending and gross private fixed investment, increased 5.8 percent in the third quarter, revised up 0.9 percentage point from the previous estimate. The price index for gross domestic purchases increased 2.7 percent in the third quarter, revised down 0.3 percentage point from the previous estimate. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index increased 2.1 percent, and the PCE price index, excluding food and energy increased 2.5 percent, both the same as previously estimated.

items.title: Trump downplays Russia, China support for Iran during talks with US troops | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
items.excerpt: Published On 27 Nov 2026 27 Nov 2026 United States President Donald Trump has claimed Iran possesses missiles capable of reaching Europe and downplayed Russia and China’s support for Tehran while speaking to US military personnel by phone for the Thanksgiving holiday. Taking questions from reporters at his Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida on Thursday, Trump said without “peace in the Middle East”, Iran could launch nuclear attacks against Israel and other countries in the region. “We don’t need Middle East oil. But what we do need is we need peace in the Middle East,” Trump said, as OPEC ministers are scheduled to meet on Sunday to weigh 2027 oil production targets. The US president and First Lady Melania Trump called US service members deployed across the region to praise their role in the war on Iran, including personnel at the al-Dhafra airbase in the United Arab Emirates and the Prince Sultan airbase in Saudi Arabia. “Each of you is playing an essential role to protect not only our country today but future generations of Americans by ensuring that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon,” he said. When asked if the US would renew strikes on Iran, the president said: “If we do something, we will definitely hit Pickaxe Mountain.” Trump also told reporters he spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in recent days. The US is still offering Iran an opening to negotiate, according to Trump, who said: “We’re trying to be nice. We’re giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives, but I’m not sure if they are gonna take advantage of that.” He downplayed the importance of intelligence-sharing by Russia and China with Iran, amid reports that the two countries helped Tehran target US bases. “My meeting with President Xi was an incredible meeting. I think that they’re very little involved with Iran. They could get involved, but involvement to me would mean shooting, not giving them little information,” Trump said during the short news conference. “We do the same thing, by the way. And you know, when they say that they may be spying on us, well, we spy on them too,” he added. Trump’s statements come as Iran steps up attacks on US military targets across the region. On Saturday, Bahrain reported an Iranian attack on a civilian industrial facility while Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed it targeted US air defence radars in the country. Kuwait said on Thursday that an Iranian drone attack on a “vital site” killed two Italian workers and injured four others. Tehran has denied involvement in the attack.

items.title: Celeb roundup: Kabza De Small's album rollout, Miley Cyrus’s wedding and more celebrity news
items.excerpt: ## 1. Kabza De Small turns one album into a three-day release Kabza De Small is giving fans more than one project to get through this week. The amapiano DJ has unveiled a three-part release plan, with a different project arriving each day from November 25 to 27 under the banner “The King of Amapiano: The Main Event”. The rollout began with “Catalogue”, a 28-track collection featuring collaborations with DJ Stockie, Leehleza, Ntockzin and Masterpiece. The largely instrumental project also includes long-awaited tracks such as “The Amabele (Remix)”, “Mnike” and “LLM”. The centrepiece is “Tutu”, a 13-track album arrived on November 26, a day earlier than originally announced. Kabza has dedicated the project to his grandmother, whom he previously described as a phenomenal woman. The album includes the single “Impilo” featuring Mkeyz, alongside collaborations with Zwadi Yamungu, Nobuhle and Chronical Deep. A deluxe edition is scheduled for today, November 27. It is an unusually generous release week from one of amapiano’s most established names. ... Mi Casa collaborates with Murumba Pitch for festive-season single ... Mi Casa is easing into the festive season with a new collaboration that brings its familiar house sound into conversation with amapiano. The trio has released “Mawe”, featuring Murumba Pitch, as the first official single from its forthcoming seventh album, “It All Takes Time”. The track combines melodic house and Afro-house influences with the contribution of the South African dance act, known for its amapiano sound. The release arrives as J’Something, Dr Duda and Mo-T mark 15 years since their self-titled debut album, which introduced audiences to songs such as “These Streets”, “Heavenly Sent” and “La Vida”. ... ## 6. Miley Cyrus marries Maxx Morando in intimate ceremony ... Miley Cyrus has married musician Maxx Morando, sharing the first glimpse of their wedding through a series of photographs that favoured understated style over a traditional bridal spectacle. The couple tied the knot in Palm Springs on November 21, with Cyrus confirming the news on Instagram two days later. Both wore custom Saint Laurent outfits designed by the fashion house’s creative director, Anthony Vaccarello.

items.excerpt: ## Entertainment Updates Live News Today In India First things first, the big box-office clash! Ayushmann Khurrana's much-anticipated Sooraj Barjatya film Yeh Prem Mol Liya and Emraan Hashmi's Gunmaaster G9 have hit cinemas today (November 27), grabbing attention with their simultaneous theatrical release. As per a tweet by KBP Reviews, Ayushmann Khurrana's Yeh Prem Mol Liya has recorded ₹2.7 crore in Day 1 advance bookings, including blocked seats. Meanwhile, Emraan Hashmi's Gunmaaster G9 has collected ₹2 crore. This means Ayushmann's film is currently ahead of Emraan's movie in advance booking figures. > The Final Advance booking for Day 1 : #YehPremMolLiya : 2.7 Cr (With Blocks) #GunmaasterG9 : 2 Cr (With Blocks) Will be watching Yeh Prem Mol Liya, Followed by Gunmaster G9, Review out soon. Godzilla is also completing it’s Run and lifetime will be under 7 Cr India gross.

The amapiano DJ has unveiled a three-part release plan, with a different project arriving each day from November 25 to 27 under the banner “The King of Amapiano: The Main Event”. The rollout began with “Catalogue”, a 28-track collection featuring collaborations with DJ Stockie, Leehleza, Ntockzin and Masterpiece.
